tasks.title: Settings reports meet the heartbeat deadline with serialized polls and cancellable shutdown
tasks.spec: ## Repository: status, all Behavior bullets, Checks (harness and tests 1-9), and Completion evidence including delayed-answer runs A and B; Decisions D1-D4 (including D1 Two bounds and Rate above the configured one); Required behavior R1-R8; Counterexamples C1-C10; Risks; Performance impact; Security impact; Acceptance evidence (feature). Implement the poll-start/report-start deadlines, 6000 ms read reserve, bounded pollNow lane and per-poll request cancellation together. Preserve SettingsPollDeps/SettingsPoll signatures and synchronous stop, payload/endpoints/settings/public behavior, timeout 5000 and heartbeat 60000. Update docs/configuration.md and README.md's Live page settings sentence for the start-to-start cadence, 60 s report bound and two distinct bounds with a token: the next read starts at most 54 s after the previous report start; above pollMs 54000, adjacent reads are 54 to 59 s apart depending on the previous read duration, never more than the configured value, so they can be faster than configured. Preserve the configured rate when the previous read is slow enough: pollMs 55000 with 4000 ms reads gives 55000 ms spacing. Include minimum read-gap checks, exact no-token cap checks, all six cases of test 9's exact read and report-to-next-read gaps, documentation grep checks and measurement of increased request rate and CPU under delayed answers. All tests and evidence belong to this single poller lifecycle change.

acceptance.expected: RED before changing the poller: run the new suite against src/settings-poll.ts from 469a6cec495d541ab393a23637fe1fbc72f74a42 or the merge base. The 60000/1000 and 60000/4000 regression cases fail report-start gap assertions with 62000 and 68000 against literal 60000. Checks 2, 3, 4, 5, 7b, 7c and 7d expose the baseline timing/overlap/shutdown defects; all six cases of check 9 fail with read-start gaps 60000, 61000, 64000, 65000, 64000 and 59000 instead of 54000, 55000, 58000, 59000, 58000 and 55000. The four other matrix cases, check 6, 7a and both cases of 8 pass. Record baseline SHA, exact command and failing assertions for the PR. Install, compile and coverage-only errors are not red evidence.

GREEN on the fix: 0 failed tests; a focused run may still fail the global coverage threshold. Use the real exported poller with resolveSettings and an empty file layer, injected clock/timer queue, promise draining and abort-aware fetch (no real network or timer waits), including contract timeout timers. Checks 1-4 observe at least 4 report starts per case, maximum adjacent PUT /service/status/report fetch-start gap <= 60000 and maximum in-flight requests 1. Check 1 covers pollMs 60000 and DEFAULT_SETTINGS_POLL_MS with latency 0, 1000 and 4000, asserting default === 15000; minimum adjacent GET-start gaps are >= 15000 for the default and >= 54000 for pollMs 60000. Check 2 alternates read latency 0/4000 and 0/timeout at 5000. Check 3 uses read latency 0 with report latency 4000 and report timeout at 5000. Check 4 uses pollMs 120000 with latency 1000 and only protects the report bound: C6 explains why the report deadline masks removal of the poll interval cap. Expectations use literals, never imported scheduling constants as their oracle.

0 failed tests for checks 5-8; coverage gate belongs to bun run check. At pollMs 1000, hold the second read, call pollNow three times, observe no overlapping GET, then exactly 1 fresh queued poll after release; all 3 promises resolve after its report completes and the next background GET occurs after advancing 1000. With resolve throwing after its first two calls, at most 4 GETs occur in 120000 ms. Stop while idle, reading or reporting, advance 300000 ms and release held work: request signals aborted, no later fetch/apply/rearm, timer queue empty and no 'status settings report failed' shutdown log. pollNow after stop and queued pollNow after stop make 0 requests; repeated stop does not throw. Check 8 runs both pollMs 60000 and 120000 with token undefined: 0 fetches and readLocal times exactly [0, 60000, 120000, 180000, 240000, 300000] in each 300000 ms run. The 120000 case protects R5/C9: a fix that removes the cap yields [0, 120000, 240000] and must fail; baseline passes. Preserve immediate first poll/report and reports after apply attempts on read errors, timeouts, 304 and 404 through the new and existing suites.

0 failed tests for all six cases of check 9 (C10, R8); coverage gate belongs to bun run check. With a token, pollMs 60000 and report latency 0, run four cases with read latency 0, 1000, 4000 and a held read that times out at 5000. Observe at least 5 settings GET starts in each case. Every adjacent GET-start gap equals its case's literal 54000, 55000, 58000 or 59000; every GET start after the first minus the previous report start equals exactly 54000. A fifth case with pollMs 120000, read latency 4000 and report latency 0 has at least 5 GET starts, adjacent gaps exactly 58000 and GET-minus-previous-report exactly 54000. A sixth case with pollMs 55000, read latency 4000 and report latency 0 has at least 5 GET starts, adjacent gaps exactly 55000 and GET-minus-previous-report exactly 51000. The sixth case preserves the configured rate; a fix that drops min(pollMs, ...) with a token gives 58000 and must fail. Expectations are literals independent of scheduling constants. These cases distinguish report-to-next-read deadlines from read-to-read spacing and reject a fixed 54000 ms read-start schedule.

0 failed tests with all 3 existing files unchanged; a focused run may fail the global coverage threshold. Existing ETag, readiness, last-good settings, rejection, local reload, precedence and public response behavior remains covered.

exit 0; Biome, ESLint (cognitive complexity <= 15 per function), workflow lint, root/e2e typechecks and the full test suite pass with line coverage >= 0.8; public response suites pass unchanged and no gate is weakened.

acceptance.command: git diff --exit-code main -- src/settings-poll.test.ts src/server.runtime-settings.test.ts src/server.settings-churn.test.ts src/start.ts src/main.ts src/runtime-settings.ts src/settings.ts
acceptance.expected: exit 0 and empty diff; existing regression suites, synchronous shutdown wiring, report construction and settings parsing remain unchanged.

acceptance.command: git diff --check && git diff --name-only main && git diff main -- src/settings-poll.ts docs/configuration.md README.md
acceptance.expected: Whitespace check exits 0; changed paths are exactly src/settings-poll.ts, src/settings-poll.heartbeat.test.ts, docs/configuration.md and README.md. Review D1-D4: due measured from poll/report starts, fallback anchor pollStart after a pre-report throw, cap min(pollMs, 60000), delay max(0, due-now), exported REPORT_LEAD_MS = SETTINGS_TIMEOUT_MS + 1000 (6000), updated heartbeat and reserve comments, at most 1 active/1 waiting poll, no catch-up loop, shared abort signal for GET/PUT and stopped checks. Configuration docs keep D1's two bounds apart: with a token the next read starts at most 54 s after the previous report start, while above pollMs 54000 adjacent reads are 54 to 59 s apart depending on the previous read duration, never more than the configured value, so they can be faster than configured; values from 60000 up behave the same. They are faster exactly when 54000 plus the previous read time is less than pollMs (or pollMs exceeds 60000), and keep the configured rate otherwise: pollMs 55000 with 4000 ms reads gives 55000 ms spacing. The start-to-start cadence is no longer stretched by a slow api and report-start gap stays <= 60 s even with the 5000 ms read timeout. README's Live page settings sentence states the default 15000, start-to-start cadence, 54 to 59 s read spacing above 54000 never more than configured (so it can be faster), and reports after every read and at least every 60 s; the rest of that paragraph and every other README section stay unchanged. Neither document claims reads above 54000 are always faster than configured. Rate claims agree with D1: no faster than configured up to 54000; above 54000 up to 1.111 times the configured rate at 60000 and up to 2.222 times at 120000, reached with instant reads. Security impact: no; review confirms unchanged request contents, routes, auth, headers, redirect manual, validation, limits, log text, dependency pins, Dockerfile, CI and public responses.

acceptance.command: grep -nE 'every 54 s|about 54 s|at most (about )?54 s apart' README.md docs/configuration.md
acceptance.expected: exit 1 and no output; neither document promises a fixed 54 s spacing or a 54 s maximum between adjacent reads.

exit 0; each file's printed count is at least 1. Review both sentences against D1 Two bounds and R8: 54 to 59 s describes adjacent reads above pollMs 54000 with a token; the 54 s bound describes time from a report start to the next read start.

exit 0; printed count is at least 1. The literal phrase can be faster appears in the configuration docs. Review docs/configuration.md and README.md against D1 Rate above the configured one and C10: above pollMs 54000 reads can be faster than configured, but may keep the configured rate when the previous read was slow enough (pollMs 55000, read latency 4000: read-start gap 55000 and read-minus-previous-report 51000). Neither document claims reads above 54000 are always faster than configured.

Delayed-answer run A: first start a temporary fake API outside the committed change, listening on 127.0.0.1:18080, delaying every answer by 4000 ms and logging request arrival times. GET /service/status/settings returns 200 with the harness's valid revision/settings body, wire header 1 and ETag e1, then 304 on If-None-Match; PUT /service/status/report returns 204 with the wire header. Run the real status service on baseline main (or merge base) and candidate three times each for a 300000 ms window from the first settings GET. GET counts: baseline 14 +/- 1 with gaps about 23000; candidate 20 +/- 1 with gaps about 15000; PUT count equals GET count +/- 1. Sample status process utime + stime from /proc/<pid>/stat fields 14 and 15 at the first GET and 300000 ms later, converting ticks to CPU ms. Record each run's counts, request times and CPU ms, each side's median CPU ms and CPU ms per poll. Candidate median CPU exceeds baseline by at most 300 ms; expected well under 100 ms. Record fixture setup, exact commands and baseline/candidate SHAs in the PR; use only loopback and dummy credentials.

Delayed-answer run B: use the same local fake API with every answer delayed 4000 ms, on baseline main (or merge base) and candidate, until at least 4 report starts per side. First GET starts immediately and first report starts about 4000 ms later. Adjacent report-start gaps: baseline 68000 +/- 50 ms, candidate 58000 +/- 50 ms; every candidate gap < 60000. Adjacent GET-arrival gaps are baseline 68000 +/- 50 ms and candidate 58000 +/- 50 ms. Each GET arrival after the first minus the previous PUT arrival is baseline 64000 +/- 50 ms and candidate 54000 +/- 50 ms; this distinguishes read spacing from the report-to-next-read deadline. Stop with Ctrl-C and observe a clean exit. Record actual request timestamps, counts, report gaps, read gaps, read-minus-previous-report gaps, fixture setup, exact commands, SHAs and exit result in the PR.

Run 3 times on baseline main and 3 times on the candidate; record user/system CPU times and compare the medians of their sums as specified under Performance impact. Added test CPU time stays < 0.2 s. This check and the fast-local benchmark do not replace delayed-answer run A. A full Docker A/B is optional; if run, follow the spec's api bench command with identical api SHAs, --others-ref main, --b-ref status=<branch SHA>, --service-tokens and --expect-report status, and keep status load_cpu_s/RSS within the named budgets.

PR body names #844 and includes actual red/green commands and assertion output (including all six exact-spacing cases of test 9, with pollMs 55000/read latency 4000 failing on old code at 59000 and passing on the fix at read-start gap 55000 and read-minus-previous-report 51000), baseline/candidate SHAs, full check result, unchanged-suite/diff evidence, all documentation grep results and review of D1's two bounds and can-be-faster rate claim, delayed-answer runs A and B with their fixture setup, startup commands, request timestamps, counts and CPU measurements, test CPU median comparison, clean shutdown result and Security impact: no. Run A shows 14 +/- 1 versus 20 +/- 1 reads per 300000 ms and median CPU increase <= 300 ms. Run B shows baseline/candidate report gaps 68000 +/- 50 versus 58000 +/- 50 ms, baseline/candidate read gaps 68000 +/- 50 versus 58000 +/- 50 ms and baseline/candidate read-minus-previous-report gaps 64000 +/- 50 versus 54000 +/- 50 ms. CI check job is green on the PR head. No notify/shared-scheduler/pin work is included; #824 remains independent.
